display.title: Counting the Days to Matan Torah: The Lessons of Sefiras HaOmer
display.summary_short: Why we count the Omer from Pesach to Shavuos, why the Torah is truly 'ours', and how to use the days of Sefirah to get ready to receive it with joy.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given on the 26th day of the Omer. Uncle Yossi explains that Sefiras HaOmer begins on the second night of Pesach and lasts 49 days until Shavuos. Our Sages teach that the Jewish people knew they had been freed from Egypt in order to receive the Torah at Mount Sinai, so they eagerly counted each day bringing them closer. We call Shavuos 'the time of the giving of our Torah', because we alone said 'na'aseh v'nishma, we will do and we will listen', so the Torah is truly ours. The remaining days of the count are for self-improvement: showing more respect to parents, elders and teachers, and building real friendship, so that we receive the Torah with inner joy. When Hashem sees our joy, He rejoices in us too, and these joys lead to the greatest joy of all, leaving golus with Moshiach.
display.lesson: Use the days of counting the Omer to improve yourself, especially in respect and friendship, and get ready to receive the Torah with joy.
